From (A_4), Pi_delta_* is a C^1 diffeomorphism onto its image S_delta_*; this makes it a local diffeomorphism only with codomain S_delta_* and therefore implies openness only relative to S_delta_*, not that S_delta_* is open in the ambient real manifold calX. The registered smooth-polar-inverse external explicitly requires S_delta_* to be an open subset of calX. A generic counterexample to the inference is any smooth embedding/diffeomorphism onto a proper embedded image (e.g. t |-> (t,0): R -> R^2): it is a diffeomorphism and local diffeomorphism onto its image, while that image is not ambient-open. To repair this step one must either assume ambient openness (as the upstream polar-retraction contract does) or prove that Pi_delta_* is a local diffeomorphism as a map into calX, e.g. by an ambient derivative isomorphism/invariance-of-domain argument; neither is supplied here.
